name: warehouse
description: Stock levels per bin, purchase orders, picking and shipments for a small warehouse.
author: test-split author (Claude Opus 5.5 subagent), written without reading the reviewer

issues.description: The docstring says a delivery may not exceed what is still outstanding, and the error message even reports the outstanding amount, but the check compares against the full ordered quantity. A second delivery can take a line past what was ordered.
issues.fix_hint: Compare the delivered quantity with outstanding (ordered minus already received).

issues.description: Every started kilogram must be charged as a full one, but round() rounds 2.2 kg down to 2 kg, so parcels are under-billed and priced in the wrong band.
release() promises a new, empty wave but only clears the lines, not the set of orders. The next wave still counts the old orders and refuses new ones once the previous wave was full.
issues.fix_hint: Reset self._orders to an empty set in release().

issues.description: The SKU is pasted into the SQL text with an f-string, so a crafted SKU changes the query (for example returns every movement).
issues.fix_hint: Use a ? placeholder and pass the SKU as a parameter.

issues.description: The reorder rule (available stock at or below the reorder point) is implemented in purchasing.needs_reorder and again, with its own arithmetic, in reports.low_stock. The two copies will drift apart.
pack_order nests for/for/for/if/if five levels deep with a for-else; finding a parcel with room and adding a unit to it should be helpers.

decoys.anchor: f"ORDER BY {order_by} DESC, id DESC LIMIT ?"
decoys.why_it_is_fine: The f-string only inserts order_by after it has been checked against the fixed SORTABLE_COLUMNS set; the limit is passed as a bound parameter.
It iterates over a list copy of the bins (and a list of the zero SKUs), so deleting from the dicts inside the loop is safe.
